What the response sim says about our track reconstruction

<p class="meta">Living record, started 2026-10-18 (dylan-Yoga). Source: MX17_Geant <code>design/report/RECO_TRUTH_2026-10-18.md</code>; scripts and logs in <code>scratchpad/2026-10-18/reco_truth/</code>.</p>

Bottom line (so far)

  • The hits ban stands, for a different reason. Hit-time ladders are compressed (C ≈ 0.85 at 10°), but almost all

of it is the measurement's geometry (each strip averages a slice of depth; diffusion dilutes the slope). An ideal ladder with no readout reproduces the data. The neighbours' delayed copies add little on data. Waveforms remain the right basis.

  • wft is not shown to be biased on data. On det3 data it is linear to 1 % against M3 from 7° to 24°. On the sim it

is not, and the sim, not wft, is what is off. No sim-derived angle correction should go into the cosmic or beam angles.

  • The data's "|wft − M3| grows with depth" is mostly M3. wft against exact truth is 0.10–0.22 mm on vertical tracks.
  • The sim's ±1 neighbour delay (×2 too late since §10.4) closes with wet gas (as the drift velocity says) plus

a ~0.4 mm prompt lateral spread at the anode. The inter-strip coupling candidate does not, and it degrades the ladder. Y and the physical origin of the spread are open.

  • Found and fixed: the sim's channels were not on det3's connector wiring, which tore 20° tracks.
  • Scope: everything here is det3 on the cosmic bench. The SPS beam data are det4, which the sim is not configured for

(its own kernel, 62 % non-amplifying area). The method conclusions (ladder geometry, M3-dominated residuals) carry over in kind; the numbers do not.

Why

The det3 response simulation (v3 baseline, FRESH_LOOK §21) now matches the cosmic-bench data in amplitude, X/Y charge sums, inclined strip extent and the central-strip timing. It still misses the ±1 neighbour delay (sim +105..+135 ns, data +45/+60), the rise (+12 ns) and the inclined-Y peak strip. Unlike the data, it knows the truth: the gun angle (a pencil beam), the impact point, the drift depth of every electron. Three questions for the cosmic and beam reconstruction:

  1. Angle closure. Calibrate wft on the sim exactly as on data (with the true line replacing M3), reconstruct, and compare with the gun. Any bias left is a property of the method and applies to data angles too.
  2. Depth-resolved residuals. The data cluster walks 0.39 → 0.55 mm from the M3 line between mesh and cathode, and σ_θ ≈ 1.0–1.1° was called a physics floor on a toy. The sim splits diffusion from reconstruction.
  3. The hit-time ladder. RECONSTRUCTION_BASIS.md bans hit times because neighbour copies compress the time ladder by 20–30 %. Measure the compression with truth, and see how it moves with the neighbour delay.

Ground rules: sim quantities that were tuned to data (amplitude, extent, Y wings) validate nothing. Predictions are written before each run. Angles from wft are in the Geant frame (ANGLED_LADDER §1); the sim drifts at 38.0 µm/ns (Stage B log at 26.5 mm), not the data bundle's 36.6.

Found on the way: the sim's channels were not on det3's wiring

Stage B writes pad column k into decoded channel k. det3's run_config marks every connector "inverted", and wft's strip map (used by every sim-vs-data script, not only wft) reads channel j at 0.78 mm × (64·(j div 64) + 63 − j mod 64). So inside a connector the sim is read mirrored, and a track that crosses a 64-channel boundary is read as two pieces ~99 mm apart. run.py's comment called the identity a pure relabelling. That is true channel by channel, but not for anything that reads strip positions.

  • The mirror explains ANGLED_LADDER §1's sign puzzle (wft "reproducing the Geant-frame sign"): the mirror and the

depth convention cancel.

  • The sim beam sits on channels ~262–298 at 0–10° (3 % of tracks cross channel 256), but at 20° its centre moves

to ~320, a boundary, and more than a quarter of the 20° tracks are torn.

  • Effect on the published comparisons (xy_extent_m3.py, v3 baseline): nothing moves at 0° or 10°. **The 10°

extent behind the 26.5 mm column choice stands. At 20° the sim's RMS extent drops from 2.90 / 2.88 to 2.72 / 2.73 mm** (data 2.75 / 2.71): the 5 % excess at 20° was the wiring.

  • Fix: response/dream/rewire.py rewrites existing decoded files (verified: the det3 map then reads exactly

0.78 mm × pad column, and the permutation is its own inverse). New Stage B runs can write the real wiring directly with run.py --wiring connector-inverted (default stays identity so old runs reproduce).

  • Not re-checked yet: the amplitude ledgers. They use peak amplitudes and should not care, but a torn 20° track

also changes which strip is the "peak strip" if the selection is position-based.

3. The hit-time ladder

Method (reco_truth/ladder.py). Per event, in the inclined view: strips ≥ 5σ and ≥ 100 ADC, no saturated strip, ≥ 4 strips. Hit time per strip = 50 % leading edge of its own waveform. Fit time against strip position (amplitude-weighted least squares). C = fitted dt/dx ÷ true dt/dx, true = 1/(v tan θ). C = 1 is an unbiased ladder, C < 1 a compressed one. Sim: θ = gun angle, v = 38.02 µm/ns. Data (det3 long run, 490 V): θ = each event's own M3 angle, other view within 3° of vertical, v = 36.6 µm/ns.

The same fit on the production combined_hits times of the data gives C within 0.01 of the waveform estimator (10°: 0.841 / 0.818 vs 0.851 / 0.824; ladder_hits.py), so this ladder is the hits chain's ladder.

The new control: an ideal ladder with no readout at all (ideal_ladder.py). Geant4 electrons, drift and diffusion from the digitizer's own gas table, binned on 0.78 mm strips; strip time = median electron arrival time. No avalanche, induction, resistive sharing, shaper or sampling. Threshold 7 % of the brightest strip (4 % and 12 % move C by ±0.01).

Median C, time-on-position fit:

What it says:

  1. Most of the ladder compression is not the readout. With no readout, the ladder already reads 0.60 at 5°, 0.85 at 10° and 0.93 at 15°: each strip averages a slice of depth, diffusion moves charge between strips with no time correlation (a textbook errors-in-variables dilution of the slope), and the threshold trims the ends. The data sit on that curve: the readout adds nothing in X and −0.03 in Y at 10°. RECONSTRUCTION_BASIS.md is right that hit times compress the ladder, and right to use the waveforms. Its attribution of the compression to the neighbours' delayed copies is mostly wrong for this estimator: the neighbours are a few-percent effect on top of the geometry. (Not tested here: the hits chain's own per-strip depth assignment with its own t0 and v, the "own t0 and v" row of its table.)
  2. The sim's readout compresses the ladder about twice as much as the data's (−0.045 / −0.055 vs 0 / −0.03 at 10°). That is the sim's late neighbour (+105..+135 ns vs +45/+60) seen through a different observable.
  3. The coupling candidate moves the ladder the wrong way. (0.05, 15 ns) takes another 0.03–0.04 off C in both views; ρ_s 2M takes it off in Y. The data's neighbour share arrives without dragging the strips' times together; the coupling's prompt copy of the central drags them together. This is an independent vote against adopting the coupling as a fitted term (Dylan's open question, HANDOFF 10-18), and for a lateral model that makes the neighbour signal earlier without making it a copy of the central (FRESH_LOOK §21.11's reading).
  4. Y is more compressed than X in the data (0.824 vs 0.851) and the ideal ladder is symmetric, so the Y readout mixes more. That matches wft's kY > 1 on data (r06: 2.9).

Mechanism checks (archived August chain, ρ_s 2M, 30 mm, rewired; ideal at 30 mm: 0.872 / 0.965 at 10° / 20°):

  • The August chain's readout share is −0.028 against v3's −0.045. Photon feedback (new in v3) is prompt and

co-located in the model, so it does not change pulse shapes. It does make v3 1.8× brighter, matching the data, so more shared-only neighbour strips pass the absolute 100 ADC / 5σ threshold (likely, not tested). The readout share would then depend on amplitude through the threshold, and the amplitude-matched v3 is the fair comparison.

1. Angle closure: wft calibrated on the sim, scored against the gun

Method (reco_truth/sim_calib.py, closure.py). The data procedure, with the true line in place of M3: wft.calibrate's ref-pinned fit (cache of waveform windows along the reference corridor, impulse template from bright inclined strips, kernel hypers fitted with each event's p0 and w pinned to the reference), seeded from det3's production bundle calib_bundle_r06 (RC-ladder kernel, c2 = 0.6 c1), v pinned to the sim's own 38.02 µm/ns as production pins data to 36.6. Training events are spread evenly over the 12 angle points. Then t13_reco.py (seeds from the sim's own waveforms, no truth) on every point, scored against the gun angle and the event's vertex line. Frame check (frame_check.py): the right tan sign beats the flipped one by 4–9× in χ², and vertical views put the χ² minimum at zero position shift. Inclined views prefer the mesh point moved along the track by ~1.4 mm of depth, the size of a t0 / depth-origin offset. Rechecked with the sim bundle.

Two arms:

  • sim-calibrated bundle: is wft unbiased when its calibration is right? That is the method's own closure.
  • data bundle r06 as is: what the data's calibration does to sim tracks (kernel mismatch plus v 36.6 vs 38.02).

Pre-registered (2026-10-18, before any closure number):

  • sim-calibrated, inclined 10°: |tan_reco / tan_true − 1| ≤ 1 % in both views; 15–30°: ≤ 2 %. Vertical: |Δθ| ≤ 0.15°.
  • σθ at 10° (robust) 0.9–1.3°, the "physics floor" of WAVEFORM_FIRST_THREADING §12.
  • Angle constants truth would assign: kw within ±2 % of 1, |w0| ≤ 1 µm/ns (data r06 from M3: kw 1.001 / 0.990,

w0 −0.04 / −0.17).

  • r06 on sim: tan ratio 1.039 (the v ratio) ± 0.03 from the kernel mismatch.
  • Falsifier: sim-calibrated bias > 3 % at 10° in either view → wft has an intrinsic angle-scale bias that, on data,

only M3's kw hides. That would transfer to every beam angle (stage 3's k) that is not M3-calibrated.

Result, sim-calibrated arm (v3 baseline, 1200 events per point; th00 3000)

The truth-pinned calibration on the sim converged to c1 0.050 (at its floor, as on data), τ_s 185 ns, σ_s 71 ns, σ_p0 0.034 mm (at its 0.03 floor) and Dp 0.0257. Data r06: σ_p0 0.42 mm, Dp 0.0144. (Below, under "sim".)

Scored against the gun (closure_table.py). Flip = the fitted direction reversed (tan sign wrong, p0 moved ~5 mm: the mirror solution). Core = |tan_reco/tan_true − 1| ≤ 0.25. Residual = median |reco line − true line| at depth z, core events.

Pre-registration: vertical |Δθ| ≤ 0.15° and σθ 0.9–1.3° hold. The falsifier fired: the 10° bias is +4.5 % / +6.6 % (≤ 1 % predicted, > 3 % falsifies), and the scale is not even linear (+6 % at 10° to −2.5 % at 20°).

What it means. The falsifier was written to catch an intrinsic wft bias that M3's kw hides on data. The data rule that out by themselves: against M3, wft on det3 is linear to ±1 % from 7° to 24° and flips ~2 % of inclined tracks, while on the sim it swings 7 % between 10° and 20° and flips 15 % at 20°. A bias intrinsic to the method would show on data too, and it does not. The data fit wft's forward model better than the sim does. The sim's waveforms are what break the method's assumptions, and the obvious suspect is the same one as everywhere else: the sim's late neighbour (§3, FRESH_LOOK §21). So:

  • No angle correction should be carried from the sim to data. The production M3 constants stand.
  • Closure becomes a new yardstick for the sim's lateral model: a better lateral model must bring the sim's flip

fraction and linearity towards the data's. Used below.

  • 30° (|tan| 0.58) is outside anything det3 saw on the bench (no data events above |tan| 0.45); at 20° the sim flips

twice as often as the data do (0.15 vs 0.07 ± 0.03).

and 20°; the data swing 1 %), and fixing the neighbour delay (wet + σ0 420 µm) does not remove it.

(The data reproduce RECONSTRUCTION_BASIS's waveform-first row, 0.39 → 0.55, with a different estimator.)

  • On head-on tracks the data's residual is almost all M3. wft's own error against truth is 0.10–0.22 mm at every

depth; the data read 0.35–0.53. In quadrature that leaves M3 a pointing error of ~0.32 mm at 3 mm growing to ~0.5 mm at 26 mm, i.e. M3's own angle error times the lever arm. The data table's growth with depth is mostly M3's, not the reconstruction's. That is where the 0.4 mm "M3 pointing floor" came from.

  • On inclined tracks the sim's own error is 0.25–0.45 mm and grows with depth (10°–15°), because the angle error

(σθ 0.9–1.05°) multiplies the depth. For these the sim is the pessimistic case: its angles are worse than the data's (above).

  • The "physics floor" σθ ≈ 1.0–1.1° (WAVEFORM_FIRST_THREADING §12, from a toy) is confirmed on the full

simulation for vertical tracks (1.10 / 1.26°) and is 0.7–1.0° on 5–15° tracks. The data's 1.15 / 1.18° against M3 includes M3's angle error, so wft on data is at or below the floor.

Sim: wet gas + a prompt lateral spread at the anode (condor 4480262)

Why this test. Three leads point at the same place.

  • FRESH_LOOK §12: the bench drift velocity says ~1 % water, but the bench widths look dry

(D_T 463–507 µm/√cm, the dry Magboltz value). The sim runs the dry table, which is why it drifts at 38.0 µm/ns instead of the data's 36.6.

  • wft's own calibration (item 1): on data the charge cloud is already σ_p0 = 0.42 mm wide at the mesh and grows

slowly (Dp 0.0144). On the dry v3 sim it starts at 0.03 mm and grows fast (Dp 0.0257).

  • FRESH_LOOK §21.11: the data's neighbour carries its share earlier, a prompt in-phase share the sim lacks.

Hypothesis H. The gas is wet as v says, and the anode has a prompt, charge-conserving lateral spread of ~0.4 mm. Together they mimic dry widths on average while moving charge from late diffusion into an in-phase neighbour share. Tested with the 1 % H₂O Magboltz table (design/gas/drift_velocity_Ar_iC4H10_95_5_H2O_1.0.json, v 37.2 µm/ns, σ_T over 26.5 mm 506 µm vs dry 785) and Stage B's new --sigma0-um (the avalanche spread; the calib has 94 µm). Arms on the v3 recipe, det3 wiring: wet only (v3w), wet + σ0 300 µm, wet + σ0 420 µm. Pre-registration in scratchpad/2026-10-18/stageBC_w3_wetspread.sub.

Against the pre-registration:

  1. v 37.2: ✔ (Stage B log).
  2. Vertical X width: wet alone 0.52 (band 0.55–0.62, a near miss, narrower than predicted); σ0 420 µm 0.65 (band 0.63–0.72) ✔.
  3. 10° extent within ±4 %: ✔ in every arm (1.40–1.45 vs 1.46).
  4. nb(0) X ≥ 0.19 with σ0 420 µm: ✔ 0.202. ±1 delay X ≤ +120 ns: ✔ +60 (and Y +60 = data).
  5. Amplitude +3..+12 % (data/sim): ✔ +7 % X, +8 % Y.
  6. wft's truth-pinned calibration on the σ0 420 µm sim returns σ_p0 0.25–0.55 mm, Dp 0.008–0.014: ✘ failed. It returns σ_p0 0.031 mm and Dp 0.0256, and puts the extra width into the kernel's time smear (σ_s 351 ns) and kY. Wet alone: σ_p0 0.038, Dp 0.0181 (the wet Magboltz value is ~0.010). wft's σ_p0 and Dp are not clean physical readouts: they trade off against its sharing-kernel parameters. So the data bundle's 0.42 mm is no evidence for a prompt spread by itself; that leg of the motivation falls. The neighbour shapes above stand on their own.
  7. Ladder C, X at 10° (band 0.80–0.86 for σ0 420 µm): ✔ 0.817. Wet alone 0.873, σ0 300 µm 0.849. The ideal ladder must use the same gas. Ideal wet + 0.42 mm is identical to ideal dry with none (0.591 / 0.849 / 0.926 / 0.958 vs 0.601 / 0.853 / 0.928 / 0.959 at 5/10/15/20°): the ladder only sees the total width, the "mimics dry" statement in another observable. Against its own ideal, the sim's readout share at 10° goes from −0.045 (v3) to −0.032 (σ0 420 µm); the data's is 0.00 (X) / −0.03 (Y).

Falsifier not triggered. One pre-registered band failed (item 5, the wft parameters).

Reading.

  • **The ±1 neighbour delay, the sim's longest-standing mismatch (×2 since §10.4), closes with a prompt anode spread

and wet gas.** Neither ρ_s (§21.11) nor the inter-strip coupling (§21.8) did: the coupling took the delay to +105 and spoiled the ladder (§3). In X every neighbour number now matches the data to 0.01–0.02 and 15 ns, and the vertical X cluster has the data's strip count and span, which v3 never had.

  • The "widths look dry" puzzle has a reading: wet diffusion plus ~0.4 mm of prompt spread gives the dry total.

The water is real (v, FRESH_LOOK §12). The prompt spread is a phenomenological term with no mechanism in the model yet. Candidates: lateral displacement of the photon-feedback secondaries, which the model places exactly on the primary (add_feedback, "land where the primary did"). That would also explain why cloud_basics finds the data's early width growing with mesh voltage (σ0 0.3 → 0.5 mm over 425 → 505 V), since bG grows with gain. The other candidate is a wider avalanche than the 94 µm Garfield calib.

  • Y is not fixed. Y's ±1/central overshoots (0.461 vs 0.408, v3 already 0.435), the vertical Y width is a little

narrow (0.79 vs 0.84), and inclined Y gets dimmer (saturates 0.19 vs 0.33). One knob cannot fix Y's core and wings together. ρ_s acts only on Y (the stripes run along y), and on both in the same direction. The Y open problem (§21.9) stands, with this baseline as the better starting point.

  • Amplitude: the σ0 420 µm arm wants bG ≈ 0.48–0.49 instead of 0.45 (≈ 2 % per 0.01, §21.10).

v4 candidate: wet + σ0 420 µm + bG 0.48, 12 angles (condor 4480263)

Recipe: the v3 flags with --feedback-bg 0.48 --sigma0-um 420 --wiring connector-inverted, and MX17_GAS_TABLE=design/gas/drift_velocity_Ar_iC4H10_95_5_H2O_1.0.json. Truth kept.

What's next (2026-10-18 evening)

  1. Dylan's calls.
    • Coupling as a fitted term: the ladder and the neighbour delay both say no.
    • The v4 candidate (wet 1 % + σ0 420 µm + bG 0.48, det3 wiring) as the new baseline: recipe flags are in scratchpad/2026-10-18/stageBC_w4_cand.sub. It would also need a det3_v4.args recipe and MX17_GAS_TABLE in the submit environment.
  2. Origin of the prompt spread. Candidate: lateral displacement of photon-feedback secondaries (the model puts them on the primary). A --feedback-spread-um option would make the spread grow with gain, as cloud_basics sees (σ0 0.3 → 0.5 mm over 425 → 505 V). Testing it needs avalanche calibs at other mesh voltages.
  3. Y (§21.9 and above): ±1/central too high while the vertical width is a bit narrow, inclined Y too dim. Not a ρ_s problem alone.
  4. wft on the sim: the nonlinearity (above). The sim-calibrated bundle also flips 12–18 % at 20°. The data bundle doesn't, so seeding or pinning σ_s / kY in the truth-pinned fit is worth a try before reading closure numbers.
  5. Housekeeping: amplitude ledgers were not affected by the wiring (peak amplitudes only), but any older position-based 20° comparison should be rerun on rewired files (python -m response.dream.rewire IN OUT).
